Thanks for taking the time today — really appreciate the thoughtful questions from your team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned:

What we covered
- Demo highlights: streaming latencies, KV cache for conversational flows, and Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.
- Key decision areas: ownership (who signs off), procurement timeline, security evidence (SOC2, logging/audit), target latency & unit economics.

Open items we asked you to confirm
1) Economic buyer / approver for budget: who will sign off on the POC and any Dedicated capacity commit?
2) Procurement contact & typical process for supplier onboarding (contracts + security vetting).
3) Target latency and cost guardrails for the POC (p95 targets, average cost per request).
4) Deployment preference: start Hosted API or Private (VPC/on-prem) given PHI considerations.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short SLA matrix and a SOC2 evidence checklist to speed procurement.

Proposed next steps
- Tom: confirm economic buyer and procurement email by EOD Tue.
- Rishi: shadow to estimate Dedicated vs Hosted cost envelope for 10k requests/day (I’ll loop him in).
- Evelyn: prep the SOC2 evidence checklist and determine which items require legal sign-off.
- Schedule 30m follow-up next week to lock decision criteria and timeline.

If easier, we can also share a lightweight mutual action plan doc (1-pager).

Thanks —

Olga — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers from our side:

1) Economic buyer: Marlene Cortez (CFO) will sign off on budget for the POC and any committed capacity. I’ve copied her on this thread separately.
2) Procurement: procurement@edgehealth.ai is the central queue; procurement lead is usually Ana Rivera (will introduce if you need a kickoff).
3) Decision criteria: rough targets we’re discussing internally — aiming for p95 latency <= 200ms for typical 256-token generations in production-like load. Cost target is more of a business constraint: we want to estimate total inference cost per active patient request and keep it under ~$0.01 on average during POC (we realize this is coarse).
4) Deployment: we’d prefer Hosted for speed of iteration but PHI concerns may push us to Private (VPC). For the POC we want to keep data within our cloud account; if Redwood supports a Private control plane with KMS integration that may be ideal.

Procurement timeline: procurement will do an initial vendor risk assessment and request SOC2 evidence. They typically want evidence and contract redlines within 7–10 business days to move forward.

Next step: I’ll introduce Ana from procurement on Monday and loop in Marlene. Can we do a 30m follow-up Tue or Wed?

—Tom
